scientific_question: Why can common one-surface evaluations of the same persistent-memory system support apparently conflicting conclusions, and what extra diagnosis is recovered by preserving the write/exposure/uptake/outcome stage signature?

result_analysis_binding.note: R4 is a paper-level reinterpretation of already frozen evidence; it does not rewrite the historical terminal-result analysis receipt.

diagnostic_result.write_only: supports a strong persistent-state update summary but cannot establish exposure or behavioral authority
diagnostic_result.retrieval_only: supports active availability/reuse but cannot distinguish availability from policy uptake
diagnostic_result.native_endpoint_only: supports a weak/sparse end-to-end summary but cannot diagnose the failed transport stage
diagnostic_result.forced_endpoint_only: supports downstream capacity under supplied memory but cannot establish native end-to-end transport
diagnostic_result.full_stage_signature: persistent write supported; forced capacity supported; native exposure directly observed; stable first-action uptake not supported; native terminal transport sparse and heterogeneous
diagnostic_result.localized_boundary: after exposure and before stable first-action uptake

scientific_interpretation.main_gain: Stage resolution is diagnostically useful because it reduces observational aliasing between state construction, downstream capacity, native availability, policy uptake, and native outcome; it is not merely more detailed reporting.
scientific_interpretation.why_not_scalar_metric: The stage observables have different units and intervention surfaces. Diagnostic information comes from which explanations remain compatible, not from dividing stage values into a transport coefficient.
scientific_interpretation.why_not_causal_mediation: The frozen design lacks atom-level seed/noise-floor controls and forced/native intervention surfaces are not identical.
scientific_interpretation.closest_work_boundary_preserved: R4 does not reclaim generic retrieval-versus-use or lifecycle-stage decomposition as novelty; the residual remains the same-trajectory reward-conditioned intervention plus capacity/native transport diagnosis.

manuscript_repairs: Abstract now motivates the stage ladder through conflicting coarse evaluations of the same frozen system.
Introduction defines evaluation coarsening and reframes the stage signature as diagnostic disambiguation rather than a finer-grained score.
Mechanism section formalizes a projection operator Pi_A and categorical stage signature Sigma without introducing a scalar transport coefficient.
Results explain how write-only, retrieval-only, native-endpoint-only, and forced-endpoint-only summaries are reconciled by the full signature.
Related Work preserves the R3b novelty demotions while distinguishing the residual contribution from generic lifecycle naming.
Limitations state that evaluation coarsening is a diagnostic information-loss claim rather than a universal theorem.
